title: RestoreMintAtIndex4 post-condition smoke test is vacuous — proves the view renders, not that minting works
description: The post-condition smoke test in RestoreMintAtIndex4 only calls getData(OWNER) and asserts view flags. It never exercises mint(4), so it proves the mint view renders but not that minting actually works. As a result 'RESTORE COMPLETE' prints even when the mint path is broken (see M-01).
impact: Operators get a false sense of completion: the smoke test reports success while the mint path can be non-functional. The post-condition does not validate the script's stated intent (restoring minting), only that a read-only view renders.
attackPath: Script runs and reaches the post-condition.
Smoke test calls getData(OWNER) and asserts flags only.
Assertions pass regardless of whether mint(4) is callable.
'RESTORE COMPLETE' prints even when minting reverts.
recommendation: Strengthen the post-condition to simulate the mint(4) path (e.g. via a staticcall/try simulation of mint -> dispatch) and assert the pooler's minter == NFT_MINTER_V2 before declaring restore complete.
